title: Bug out: evacuation destinations, triggers and routes
tldr: A useful bug-out plan names when to leave, where to go, how to travel and what to do if the first option fails. The destination matters more than an overloaded bag.
steps: Write hazard-specific triggers: evacuation instructions, unsafe building conditions, approaching wildfire, flood access loss or inability to sustain essential care. Leave before routes become unsafe where possible.
Arrange a nearby and an outside-area destination. Check acceptance, accessibility, pets, parking and essential care. An unconfirmed shelter or public campground is not a guaranteed destination.
Map at least two practical routes where available. Consider no-car travel, fuel, road closures, bridges, water hazards and travel time with dependents.
Prioritize medicines, identification, contacts, mobility aids, keys, phone power, water and weather protection. Assign bags and dependent care; never delay an urgent departure to complete packing.
sections: For each likely hazard record the trigger, destination and transport owner. Add who checks current conditions and how the household receives the decision. Avoid a vague promise to “head to the woods”: unfamiliar land, missing shelter, property restrictions and water uncertainty can make that move worse than an established destination.

Use the alternate destination and route agreed ahead of time. If a road is flooded, closed or affected by active danger, do not force a crossing. Tell your contact where you are going if it is safe to communicate. If no safe route remains, seek the best available protective location for the actual hazard and reassess; do not treat staying as universally safe.
without_help: Work from confirmed reachable options and supplies already accessible. Help may be delayed, so keep your own contacts, route notes and essential care information available without internet.
household: Assign an adult to each dependent and identify who can drive or arrange accessible transport. Check shelter rules for pets, service animals and support equipment before an event.
pack_now: Keep the equipment and written information described above where the responsible person can reach them. Test access in darkness, with a tired household, and while carrying the items you actually need.
next: Time a calm departure rehearsal with the actual people, bags and transport. Record the slowest step and fix it.
watch: No universal bug-out destination or timetable suits every disaster. Avoid flooded roads and do not enter an active danger area for supplies.
review_status: Source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
faqs: No. Check that it fits the intended task, can be used by the people who need it, and has a maintenance plan. Practice in safe conditions before relying on it.
scope: Civilian educational planning. References include U.S. systems; local laws, conditions and services differ.
